title.narrative: Newton001: Research and Training in Leishmaniasis, a Neglected Tropical Disease of Public Health Importance in Brazil

description.narrative: The Newton Fund builds research and innovation partnerships with developing countries across the world to promote the economic development and social welfare of the partner countries.

To enhance research links between the UK and Brazil in the molecular, cell and immunobiology of Leishmania parasites, which cause the Neglected Disease leishmaniaisis, and their interaction with the mammalian host. To provide advanced skills training in state of-the-art in vivo imaging, RNA-seq and novel concepts in computer modelling of infection to drug development and the understanding of pathogenesis of leishmaniasis. This will address specific skills shortages in Brazil and highlight the reduction and refinement of animals in scientific research. To provide residential advanced training in Rio de Janeiro to integrate UK and Brazilian experts in in vivo imaging, advanced meta-approaches of genomics/transcriptome and computational modelling. This will allow established investigators and early career scientists to interact and will offer the opportunity for people with common research interests to develop new projects. To develop hypotheses and generate pilot data in Brazil that will underpin future research collaboration and funding applications.
